name: si-units

description.en: The International System of Units (SI) in 53 cards: the 7 base units, the 22 derived units with special names and the 24 SI prefixes, including ronna, quetta, ronto and quecto from 2022. The front names a quantity or a prefix; the back gives the SI unit with its symbol, or the prefix's factor and symbol. Compiled from NIST's SI guide and prefix table, Swedac's regulations on units of measurement (STAFS 2009:26) and Wikidata, and checked against the BIPM SI Brochure.
description.sv: Internationella måttenhetssystemet (SI) i 53 kort: de 7 grundenheterna, de 22 härledda enheterna med särskilda namn och de 24 SI-prefixen, inklusive ronna, quetta, ronto och quekto från 2022. Framsidan anger en storhet eller ett prefix; baksidan ger SI-enheten och dess beteckning, eller prefixets faktor och beteckning. Sammanställd ur NIST:s SI-guide och prefixtabell, Swedacs föreskrifter om måttenheter (STAFS 2009:26) och Wikidata, och kontrollerad mot BIPM:s SI-broschyr.

method: Research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction, with machine checks (this builder's Wikidata checks and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators); review rounds by independent AI reviewers are logged under Quality control. No human subject expert has reviewed the cards yet.

Units in English: downloaded NIST SP 811 (2008) as PDF and extracted its text with pypdf. Table 1 (SI base units, PDF p. 16) gave the 7 base units and Table 3 ("The 22 SI coherent derived units with special names and symbols", PDF p. 17) the 22 derived units: for each, the quantity, the unit name and the symbol. Where a row names several quantities ("energy, work, amount of heat") the card names the first one, which is unique among the 29 units.
Prefixes: downloaded NIST's Metric (SI) Prefixes page and read its table of 24 prefixes (name, symbol, factor 10^30 to 10^−30). The deck uses all 24.

Swedish: downloaded the consolidated Swedac regulation STAFS 2009:26 om måttenheter (amended up to STAFS 2020:2) and extracted its text. Bilaga 1.1 (SI-grundenheter), 1.1.1 (Celsiustemperatur), 1.2.3 (Härledda SI-enheter med särskilda namn och beteckningar) and 1.3 (Multipelprefix) gave the Swedish quantity names, unit names and the 20 prefixes it lists (hekto, deka, mikro, piko, yokto ...). Where STAFS names several quantities for one unit the card uses the one that matches the English front ("elektrisk laddning", "elektrisk spänning").

The four prefixes adopted in 2022 (ronna, quetta, ronto, quecto) are not in STAFS 2009:26. Their Swedish names were taken from the Swedish labels of their Wikidata items (ronna, quetta, ronto, quekto) and checked against the prefix table of Swedish Wikipedia (Mall:SI-prefix: Quetta, Ronna, Ronto, Quekto).

Wikidata: SPARQL queries (see Queries) fetched, for the 29 units, their English and Swedish labels and aliases, unit symbols (P5061) and measured quantities (P111) with the quantities' labels; and for every item that is an instance of SI prefix (Q131299), its labels, symbol (P5061) and numeric value (P1181). English unit names follow the international (BIPM and Wikidata) spelling: metre, deca; NIST's US spellings meter and deka are given in a note.

Card text: fronts read "SI unit of <quantity>" / "SI-enhet för <storhet>" for units and the bare prefix name with the note "SI prefix" for prefixes. Backs give the unit name and symbol, "newton (N)", in English and Swedish, or the factor and symbol of a prefix, "10³ (k)", untagged since it has no language. The micro sign is the Greek letter μ (U+03BC), as on NIST's page and in Wikidata. Unit names are lower case, as the SI requires; "Celsius" keeps its capital. Notes say whether a unit is a base unit or a derived unit with a special name, and point out the pairs that share a dimension (Hz and Bq, Gy and Sv). Further notes: the radian and steradian notes follow the current BIPM brochure (Section 2.3.3: plane and solid angle are treated as quantities with the unit one by convention), backed by NIST SP 811 Table 3 (expressed as 1), after QC round 1 found SP 811's 2008 wording out of date; the degree Celsius note (equal to the kelvin, t/°C = T/K − 273.15) comes from NIST SP 811 Section 4.2.1.1 and STAFS bilaga 1.1.1; kilo's lower-case symbol from NIST's prefix page (Capitalization), checked against BIPM Section 3.1; the year 2022 and the four prefixes added together from NIST's prefix page (Prefix Progress table), checked against Wikidata P571 and BIPM Resolution 3 of the 27th CGPM; the alternative Swedish names of illuminance (belysningsstyrka, illuminans) from Wikidata Q194411; the US spellings meter and deka from NIST.

Cross-check: every card was compared against the BIPM SI Brochure (9th edition, V4.01, June 2026; Table 2 base units, Table 4 the 22 derived units, Table 7 the 24 prefixes, and Resolution 3 of the 27th CGPM for the 2022 prefixes) and against Wikidata through the builder's machine checks: the English and Swedish label of each unit and prefix, its symbol, each prefix's numeric value and SI-prefix class, each unit's measured quantity, and the English and Swedish labels of the quantities wherever Wikidata uses the card's wording. Where Wikidata disagreed with the official sources the check was left out and the discrepancy recorded (Quality control, round 0).

Not used: NIST SP 330 (2019), the US edition of the SI Brochure, was downloaded (see Queries) and read for its licence only: it carries the BIPM's note that "All BIPM's works are internationally protected by copyright", so it is not a public-domain source, and it predates the 2022 prefixes.

Swedish forms of the 2022 prefixes: no Swedish regulation or authority lists them yet (STAFS 2009:26 stops at yotta and yokto), so 'ronna', 'quetta', 'ronto' and 'quekto' rest on Wikidata's Swedish labels and Swedish Wikipedia only. The quekto card says so in its Swedish note. The web search behind this claim was not logged at authoring; in QC round 4 it was re-run on 2026-10-04 (two web searches, terms under Queries). Neither found guidance from Swedac, RISE or Språkrådet on Swedish forms of the 2022 prefixes. The second listed STAFS 2022:6, which was downloaded and checked: it amends STAFS 2016:1 on measuring instruments, not STAFS 2009:26, and the consolidated STAFS 2009:26 still ends at the amendment STAFS 2020:2.

Text extraction: PDFs with pypdf and the NIST HTML pages with Beautiful Soup (see Queries). The original extraction commands were not logged in full during authoring; in QC round 3 the commands listed under Queries were re-run on 2026-10-04 and produce the text files used for the cards byte for byte, and the re-downloaded NIST SP 330 PDF has the same SHA-256 as the copy read at authoring.
selection: All of the core SI: the 7 base units, the 22 derived units with special names and symbols (as listed in NIST SP 811 Table 3 and BIPM SI Brochure Table 4, including the radian, steradian, degree Celsius and katal), and the 24 SI prefixes from quetta (10³⁰) to quecto (10⁻³⁰) as listed by NIST. Left out: derived units without special names (square metre, metre per second ...), non-SI units accepted for use with the SI (litre, tonne, minute, electronvolt ...), the binary prefixes (kibi, mebi ...), which are IEC, not SI, and the defining constants. One card per unit and per prefix; for units with several quantities the first quantity named in the tables is on the front.

rounds.lens: Source agreement and machine checks: every card against NIST (SP 811, prefix page), Swedac STAFS 2009:26, the BIPM SI Brochure and Wikidata.
rounds.scope: All 53 cards; the licences of all sources.
rounds.summary: 276 Wikidata checks pass (python3 scripts/authored_decks.py check si-units, 2026-10-04): for every unit its English label, Swedish label (except two, below), symbol (P5061) and, for 27 units, measured quantity (P111); for every prefix its English and Swedish label, symbol, numeric value (P1181) and class SI prefix (Q131299); and the English or Swedish label of the quantity on the front wherever Wikidata uses the card's wording. All 29 units and 24 prefixes agree in name, symbol and factor across NIST, the BIPM brochure and Wikidata; the Swedish unit and prefix names agree between STAFS 2009:26 and Wikidata except where noted. Discrepancies and how they were resolved are listed as findings; no check was dropped to make the build pass other than those listed.

findings.issue: Wikidata Q208634's Swedish label is 'Katal' (capitalised); STAFS 2009:26 has 'katal', and SI unit names are written in lower case.
findings.resolution: Kept 'katal' (STAFS); no Swedish label check for this card.

findings.issue: Wikidata Q25267's Swedish label is the plural 'grader Celsius', and its aliases do not include the singular; STAFS 2009:26 names the unit 'grad Celsius'.
findings.resolution: Kept 'grad Celsius' (STAFS), singular like every other unit name on the cards; no Swedish label check for this card.

findings.issue: Wikidata gives the measured quantity of the second as duration (Q2199864); NIST SP 811, STAFS and BIPM call the base quantity 'time' / 'tid'.
findings.resolution: Kept 'time' / 'tid'; no P111 check for this card.

findings.issue: Wikidata gives the radian's measured quantity (P111) as Q1357788, whose English label is 'angular measure' with 'plane angle' only as an English alias, and whose Swedish label is 'vinkelavstånd' (angular distance); NIST, STAFS and BIPM say 'plane angle' / 'plan vinkel'. (Wording made precise in round 5.)
findings.resolution: Kept 'plane angle' / 'plan vinkel'. Since round 5 the P111 value and the English alias 'plane angle' are checked; the Swedish quantity label is not checked because Wikidata's 'vinkelavstånd' does not match STAFS's 'plan vinkel'.

findings.issue: Swedish name of the quantity: STAFS 'elektrisk ström', Wikidata Q29996 'elektrisk strömstyrka'.
findings.resolution: Front uses STAFS's 'elektrisk ström'; only the English quantity label is checked.

findings.issue: Swedish name of the quantity: STAFS 'termodynamisk temperatur', Wikidata Q264647 'absolut temperatur'.
findings.resolution: Front uses STAFS's 'termodynamisk temperatur'; only the English quantity label is checked.

findings.issue: Swedish name of the quantity: STAFS 'belysning', Wikidata Q194411 'illuminans'.
findings.resolution: Front uses STAFS's 'belysning'; only the English quantity label is checked.

findings.issue: English quantity: NIST and BIPM 'electric resistance', Wikidata Q25358 'electrical resistance'.
findings.resolution: Front follows NIST and BIPM; only the Swedish quantity label ('resistans') is checked.

findings.issue: English quantity: NIST and BIPM 'electric conductance', Wikidata Q309017 'electrical conductance'.
findings.resolution: Front follows NIST and BIPM; only the Swedish quantity label ('konduktans') is checked.

findings.issue: Wikidata Q215313's Swedish label is 'Absorberad dos' (capitalised); STAFS has 'Absorberad dos (inom radiologin)' at the start of a table row.
findings.resolution: Front uses 'absorberad dos' in lower case, as it stands mid-phrase; only the English quantity label is checked.

findings.issue: The quantity is 'activity referred to a radionuclide' (NIST, BIPM) and 'Aktivitet (inom radiologin)' (STAFS); a literal front would be long.
findings.resolution: Front reads 'SI unit of activity of a radionuclide' / 'SI-enhet för aktivitet hos en radionuklid' (own wording); the Swedish quantity label 'aktivitet' (Q317949) is checked.

findings.issue: Spelling: NIST (US) 'meter', BIPM and Wikidata 'metre'.
findings.resolution: English back uses the international 'metre (m)'; the note gives the US spelling.

findings.issue: Spelling: NIST (US) 'deka', BIPM and Wikidata 'deca'; Swedish 'deka' (STAFS, Wikidata).
findings.resolution: English front 'deca', Swedish 'deka'; the note gives the US spelling.

findings.issue: Code point of the micro symbol: NIST's page and Wikidata use Greek mu U+03BC, the BIPM PDF's text layer has the micro sign U+00B5, and STAFS's text layer has lost the glyph. They look the same.
findings.resolution: Used U+03BC, so that the Wikidata symbol check compares the same character.

findings.issue: No Swedish regulation lists the 2022 prefixes yet (STAFS 2009:26 is consolidated only up to STAFS 2020:2 and has 20 prefixes), so the Swedish spelling 'quekto' rests on Wikidata and Swedish Wikipedia, not on an official Swedish source. It follows the pattern of yokto, piko, mikro, hekto.
findings.resolution: Kept 'quekto' (Wikidata label, Swedish Wikipedia's prefix table); recorded as an open question for a human reviewer.

findings.issue: The Swedish names of ronna, quetta and ronto likewise come from Wikidata and Swedish Wikipedia only; they are spelt as in English.
findings.resolution: Kept; same as for quekto.

findings.issue: Wikidata Q154108's English label is 'milli-' with a hyphen.
findings.resolution: The card uses 'milli' (NIST, BIPM); the builder's label check finds 'milli' among the item's English labels or aliases, so it passes.

findings.issue: The brief named NIST SP 330 as a public-domain content source, but SP 330 (2019) reproduces the BIPM text with the BIPM's note 'All BIPM's works are internationally protected by copyright', and it predates the 2022 prefixes.
findings.resolution: Not used. NIST SP 811 (a NIST-authored work) and NIST's prefix page are the NIST content sources instead.

findings.issue: The brief believed the BIPM SI Brochure to be CC BY 3.0 IGO; the current edition (V4.01, June 2026) states CC BY 4.0.
findings.resolution: Recorded as CC BY 4.0 and used for verification only, so the deck can stay CC0.

rounds.scope: All 53 cards, against the BIPM SI Brochure (V4.01, June 2026), NIST's prefix page and STAFS 2009:26; the builder's Wikidata checks re-run.
rounds.summary: No factual errors in fronts or backs. The radian and steradian notes used NIST SP 811's 2008 wording ("a special name for the number one"), which the current BIPM brochure no longer uses; both notes now follow BIPM Section 2.3.3. The Swedish 'quekto' has no official Swedish source; the card now says so. Two optional notes (Celsius, lux) were added. All findings verified against the scratch copies of the sources and applied.

findings.issue: The note 'a special name for the number one' comes only from NIST SP 811 (2008), note (b); the current BIPM brochure says the representation rad = m/m 'is not intrinsic and may be misleading' and that angles are treated as quantities with the unit one 'for reasons of history and convention' (Section 2.3.3).
findings.resolution: Verified in the BIPM text (Section 2.3.3, PDF p. 22; Table 4 footnote (b), PDF p. 24). Note changed to "One of the 22 SI derived units with special names. By convention the SI treats plane angle as a quantity with the unit one." / "… Inom SI behandlas plan vinkel av konvention som en storhet med enheten ett." Evidence: SP 811 Table 3 (expressed as 1) with BIPM Section 2.3.3 and footnote (b).

findings.issue: Same out-of-date 'number one' note as the radian; BIPM Table 4 footnote (c) says sr = m²/m² 'is not intrinsic and may be misleading'.
findings.resolution: Verified (BIPM Table 4 footnote (c), PDF p. 24). Note changed in the same way, for solid angle / rymdvinkel; evidence as for the radian.

findings.issue: The Swedish 'quekto' rests only on Wikidata and sv.wikipedia; STAFS 2009:26 (to 2020:2) predates 2022 and no Swedish authority confirms the spelling.
findings.resolution: Confirmed: STAFS's prefix table stops at yotta and yokto. Kept 'quekto' and added to the Swedish note: "Stavningen quekto följer mönstret yokto och piko; Swedacs föreskrifter tar ännu inte upp prefixet. Internationellt: quecto." STAFS bilaga 1.3 added as evidence; the lack of an official Swedish source was already in round 0 and is now also a method step.

findings.issue: The front contains 'Celsius', so it gives most of the answer away; suggested a note that teaches something.
findings.resolution: Added the note "Equal in size to the kelvin: t/°C = T/K − 273.15." / "Lika stor som kelvin: t/°C = T/K − 273,15." with evidence from NIST SP 811 (Section 4.2.1.1, Appendix B.8), STAFS bilaga 1.1.1 and BIPM Section 2.3.1.
